facts.raw_span: A 61-year-old man presented with gross hematuria
Intravenous urography demonstrated a tubular filling defect with partial obstruction of the right mid ureter
Retrograde ureteropyelography confirmed a 5 cm long tubular mass in the mid ureter proximal to the iliac vessels
Urine cytology and endoscopic biopsy of the lesion and renal pelvis were negative for malignancy
A staging CT scan showed slight dilatation of the right renal pelvis and subtle thickening of the right ureter without evidence of metastasis or lymphadenopathy

concepts.why: Intravenous urography and retrograde ureteropyelography demonstrated a tubular filling defect and a 5 cm long tubular mass in the mid ureter, respectively, which is consistent with a ureteral polyp.

aliases: Transitional cell carcinoma of the ureter
concepts.why: Although urine cytology and endoscopic biopsy were negative for malignancy, the presence of a tubular mass in the ureter raises the possibility of ureteral carcinoma.
The partial obstruction of the right mid ureter and the slight dilatation of the right renal pelvis suggest a possible ureteral stricture.
The patient's presentation with gross hematuria and microscopic hematuria is consistent with nephrolithiasis, although no stones were directly visualized.
The patient's intermittent right pelvic pain and the presence of a tubular filling defect in the ureter suggest possible ureteritis.
The ureteral mass could be a fibroepithelial polyp, which is a benign tumor.
The ureteral mass could be a papilloma, which is a type of benign tumor.
The ureteral mass could be a hemangioma, which is a benign vascular tumor.

rationales.F01: Gross hematuria is a common symptom of ureteral polyps and carcinomas.
rationales.F06: A 60-pack-year smoking history increases the risk of ureteral carcinoma.
rationales.F09: Intravenous urography demonstrating a tubular filling defect with partial obstruction of the right mid ureter is highly suggestive of a ureteral polyp or carcinoma.
rationales.F10: Retrograde ureteropyelography confirming a 5 cm long tubular mass in the mid ureter proximal to the iliac vessels is highly suggestive of a ureteral polyp or carcinoma.
rationales.F11: Negative urine cytology and endoscopic biopsy results make ureteral carcinoma less likely.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's presentation with gross hematuria and microscopic hematuria, along with the imaging findings of a tubular filling defect and a pedunculated ureteral tumor, are most consistent with a ureteral fibroepithelial polyp, which is a benign tumor that can cause obstructive symptoms and bleeding.
